summary: Edward Burnett Tylor studied at Grove House School and worked in religious studies and other fields. He held posts at the University of Seville and the University of Oxford (~1883-1909), and taught Marcel Mauss.

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Magdalen College and the University of Oxford (1850-1854) under Horace Hayman Wilson. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian studies, he held posts at Presidency College, Calcutta, and Cambridge (1867-1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr., an Indologist and scholar of religion, studied at Harvard (Ph.D. ~1954-1959) and Yale. He served as assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972-1986).

Edward Capps, active in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Illinois College (1887-1888), Yale University (1890-1907), and Princeton University (1907-1936).

Edward Clive Bayley worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and the East India Company College (~1840-1842), and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, Kiel, Cologne (Ph.D.), Hamburg, and Bonn under Max Walleser and Max Scheler. He held posts at London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, Berkeley, and Lancaster.

Edward Delavan Perry worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University (A.B. ~1871-1875) and the University of Tübingen (Dr. phil. ~1877-1879), and served as Jay Professor at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross studied at University College London and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke. A scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the British Museum, and SOAS (1916-1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and under Woolsey, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Burnouf, Bopp, and Lassen. Active in Indology and linguistics, he was professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841-1854) and president of AOS.

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett works in computational linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at UCLA (~1995-2001) under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and held research assistant posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Granville Browne studied at Newcastle, Cambridge, and St Bartholomew's under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. A scholar of Iranian studies, linguistics, and history, he became lecturer in Persian and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Edward H. Schafer was a Sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He was a faculty member in Oriental Languages at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947-1984) and president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Hamilton Johnston studied at Eton College and New College. Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909-1924) and as a professor at the University of Oxford (~1937-1942).

Edward James Rapson studied at Hereford Cathedral School and St John's College, Cambridge. A scholar of Indology, history, and linguistics, he held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1906-1936).

Edward Joseph Thomas, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a master's at St Andrews under John Burnet and studied at Cambridge. From ~1909 to 1939, he served at Cambridge University Library and as departmental dean at Cambridge.

Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (~1970-1982) and held faculty appointments there from ~1986 to 2021, where he became Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Philosopher Edward S. Casey studied at Yale, Northwestern (Ph.D.), and Paris under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, Yale, and Stony Brook University, where he was dean of philosophy, and served as president of the APA.

Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (~1910-1925) and taught at the University of Chicago (~1925-1931) and Yale University (~1931-1939).

Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Between approximately 1824 and 1834, he was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.
